summary: Wilhelm K. Essler works in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Munich (~1960–1966) under Wilhelm Britzelmayr and Wolfgang Stegmüller, later serving as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1986–2005).

Wilhelm Max Müller was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1885) and the University of Leipzig (~1885–1888), later holding a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1918–1919).

Wilhelm Pertsch worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1851–1853) under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding leadership posts at Gotha's library and coin cabinet.
Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Wilhelm Schulze (~1906–1911) and Heinrich Lüders (~1909–1911).

Wilhelm Rau was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller (~1941–1945) and Marburg under Johannes Nobel (1946–1949). He was a professor at Frankfurt (1955) and Ordinarius at Marburg (1958–1987).

Wilhelm Roscher studied at the University of Göttingen (~1835–1838) and Frederick William University Berlin (~1838–1840). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1840–1848), University of Leipzig (~1848–1894), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Wilhelm Scherer worked in linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1858–1862) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1860) under Moriz Haupt, Franz Bopp, and Karl Müllenhoff, later holding chairs at Vienna (1868–1872), Strasbourg (1872), and Berlin (1877).

Wilhelm Schmidt worked in linguistics and religious studies. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1895), he held posts at the University of Vienna (~1921–1938) and the University of Fribourg (~1939–1951).

Wilhelm Schott specialized in Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1823–1826) and subsequently held a post there from ~1838 to 1889.

Wilhelm Schulze worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Berlin and Greifswald under Johannes Schmidt and Heinrich Zimmer. He held chairs at the University of Marburg (1892), University of Göttingen (1895), and Humboldt University of Berlin (1902–1932).
Wilhelm Solf studied Indology under Richard Pischel at Halle-Wittenberg (~1882–1885), with additional studies at Berlin, Göttingen, Kiel, and Jena. He held a post at Kiel University (~1887–1888).
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp (~1851–1854) and Moriz Haupt (~1853–1856).

Wilhelm Streitberg was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Münster, Leipzig (under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch), and Berlin. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889–1899), Münster (1899), Munich (1909–1920), and Leipzig (1898, 1920–1925).

Wilhelm Vatke specialized in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg (~1824–1826), Göttingen (~1826–1827), and Berlin (~1827–1829), later holding a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1834–1882).

Wilhelm Wackernagel worked in linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh, and later served on the faculty at the University of Basel (1833; 1835–1869).

Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy. He studied at Tübingen (~1851–1852), Heidelberg (~1852–1855), and Berlin (~1856), and later held posts at the University of Zurich (1857), University of Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen, and Jena under teachers including Lichtenberg and Heyne, and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809–1810), which he founded.

Will Sweetman is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University (~1989–1993) and the University of Cambridge (~1993–1997), and held a post at the University of Otago (~2004).

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby was a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard, and held posts at McGill (1960–1964), Yale (1966–1971), and the University of Toronto and Trinity College (~1971–1999).

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher who studied at Oberlin College (1926–1930) and Harvard University (1930–1931). He held an Assistant Professorship at Harvard (1940–1978) and visiting posts at Oxford (~1953–1954) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).
